USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Avoiding a dangerous examination

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A frightened child with suspected epiglottitis remains upright on a parent’s lap and becomes distressed when approached. Stridor is audible. Which initial approach best reduces the risk of sudden airway deterioration while expert help is mobilized?

  1. Minimize handling and allow the preferred position
  2. Force supine positioning for a throat swab
  3. Perform repeated tongue-depressor examinations
  4. Give an oral sedative before airway assessment
  5. Send the child unaccompanied for neck radiography
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Minimize handling and allow the preferred position

Agitation, forced positioning and pharyngeal stimulation can worsen a precarious airway.

Understanding the options

Minimize handling and allow the preferred position
Agitation, forced positioning and pharyngeal stimulation can worsen a precarious airway.
Force supine positioning for a throat swab
Forced positioning and swabbing may precipitate obstruction.
Perform repeated tongue-depressor examinations
Repeated pharyngeal stimulation is unsafe without definitive airway readiness.
Give an oral sedative before airway assessment
Sedation can impair compensatory tone and ventilation.
Send the child unaccompanied for neck radiography
An unstable airway should not be transported without appropriate support.
